28const MAX_AVG_VARIANCE: f32 = 0.38;
29const MAX_INDIVIDUAL_VARIANCE: f32 = 0.5;
30
31const W: u32 = 3; // Pixel width of a 3x wide line
32const W_LOWER: u32 = 2; // Pixel width of a 2x wide line
33const N: u32 = 1; // Pixed width of a narrow line
34
35/** Valid ITF lengths. Anything longer than the largest value is also allowed. */
36const DEFAULT_ALLOWED_LENGTHS: [u32; 5] = [6, 8, 10, 12, 14];
37
38/**
39 * Start/end guard pattern.
40 *
41 * Note: The end pattern is reversed because the row is reversed before
42 * searching for the END_PATTERN
43 */
44const START_PATTERN: [u32; 4] = [N, N, N, N];
45const END_PATTERN_REVERSED: [[u32; 3]; 2] = [
46    [N, N, W_LOWER], // 2x
47    [N, N, W],       // 3x
48];
49
50// See ITFWriter.PATTERNS
51
52/**
53 * Patterns of Wide / Narrow lines to indicate each digit
54 */
55const PATTERNS: [[u32; 5]; 20] = [
56    [N, N, W_LOWER, W_LOWER, N], // 0
57    [W_LOWER, N, N, N, W_LOWER], // 1
58    [N, W_LOWER, N, N, W_LOWER], // 2
59    [W_LOWER, W_LOWER, N, N, N], // 3
60    [N, N, W_LOWER, N, W_LOWER], // 4
61    [W_LOWER, N, W_LOWER, N, N], // 5
62    [N, W_LOWER, W_LOWER, N, N], // 6
63    [N, N, N, W_LOWER, W_LOWER], // 7
64    [W_LOWER, N, N, W_LOWER, N], // 8
65    [N, W_LOWER, N, W_LOWER, N], // 9
66    [N, N, W, W, N],             // 0
67    [W, N, N, N, W],             // 1
68    [N, W, N, N, W],             // 2
69    [W, W, N, N, N],             // 3
70    [N, N, W, N, W],             // 4
71    [W, N, W, N, N],             // 5
72    [N, W, W, N, N],             // 6
73    [N, N, N, W, W],             // 7
74    [W, N, N, W, N],             // 8
75    [N, W, N, W, N],             // 9
76];
77
78/**
79 * <p>Implements decoding of the ITF format, or Interleaved Two of Five.</p>
80 *
81 * <p>This Reader will scan ITF barcodes of certain lengths only.
82 * At the moment it reads length 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, and 44 as these have appeared "in the wild". Not all
83 * lengths are scanned, especially shorter ones, to avoid false positives. This in turn is due to a lack of
84 * required checksum function.</p>
85 *
86 * <p>The checksum is optional and is not applied by this Reader. The consumer of the decoded
87 * value will have to apply a checksum if required.</p>
88 *
89 * <p><a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interleaved_2_of_5">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interleaved_2_of_5</a>
90 * is a great reference for Interleaved 2 of 5 information.</p>
91 *
92 * @author kevin.osullivan@sita.aero, SITA Lab.
93 */
94#[derive(OneDReader)]
95pub struct ITFReader {
96    // Stores the actual narrow line width of the image being decoded.
97    narrowLineWidth: i32,
98}
99
100impl Default for ITFReader {
101    fn default() -> Self {
102        Self {
103            narrowLineWidth: -1,
104        }
105    }
106}
107
108impl OneDReader for ITFReader {
109    fn decode_row(
110        &mut self,
111        rowNumber: u32,
112        row: &crate::common::BitArray,
113        hints: &crate::DecodeHints,
114    ) -> Result<crate::RXingResult> {
115        // Find out where the Middle section (payload) starts & ends
116        let mut row = row.clone();
117        let startRange = self.decodeStart(&row)?;
118        let endRange = self.decodeEnd(&mut row)?;
119
120        let mut result = String::with_capacity(20); //new StringBuilder(20);
121        self.decodeMiddle(&row, startRange[1], endRange[0], &mut result)?;
122        let resultString = result; //.toString();
123
124        let allowedLengths = if let Some(al) = &hints.AllowedLengths {
125            al.clone()
126        } else {
127            DEFAULT_ALLOWED_LENGTHS.to_vec()
128        };
129
130        // To avoid false positives with 2D barcodes (and other patterns), make
131        // an assumption that the decoded string must be a 'standard' length if it's short
132        let length = resultString.chars().count();
133        let mut lengthOK = false;
134        let mut maxAllowedLength = 0;
135        for allowedLength in allowedLengths {
136            if length == allowedLength as usize {
137                lengthOK = true;
138                break;
139            }
140            maxAllowedLength = std::cmp::max(allowedLength, maxAllowedLength);
141        }
142        if !lengthOK && length > maxAllowedLength as usize {
143            lengthOK = true;
144        }
145        if !lengthOK {
146            return Err(Exceptions::FORMAT);
147        }
148
149        let mut resultObject = RXingResult::new(
150            &resultString,
151            Vec::new(), // no natural byte representation for these barcodes
152            vec![
153                point(startRange[1] as f32, rowNumber as f32),
154                point(endRange[0] as f32, rowNumber as f32),
155            ],
156            BarcodeFormat::ITF,
157        );
158
159        resultObject.putMetadata(
160            RXingResultMetadataType::SYMBOLOGY_IDENTIFIER,
161            RXingResultMetadataValue::SymbologyIdentifier("]I0".to_owned()),
162        );
163
164        Ok(resultObject)
165    }
166}
167impl ITFReader {
168    /**
169     * @param row          row of black/white values to search
170     * @param payloadStart offset of start pattern
171     * @param resultString {@link StringBuilder} to append decoded chars to
172     * @throws NotFoundException if decoding could not complete successfully
173     */
174    fn decodeMiddle(
175        &self,
176        row: &BitArray,
177        payloadStart: usize,
178        payloadEnd: usize,
179        resultString: &mut String,
180    ) -> Result<()> {
181        let mut payloadStart = payloadStart;
182        // Digits are interleaved in pairs - 5 black lines for one digit, and the
183        // 5 interleaved white lines for the second digit.
184        // Therefore, need to scan 10 lines and then
185        // split these into two arrays
186        let mut counterDigitPair = [0_u32; 10]; //new int[10];
187        let mut counterBlack = [0_u32; 5]; //new int[5];
188        let mut counterWhite = [0_u32; 5]; //new int[5];
189
190        while payloadStart < payloadEnd {
191            // Get 10 runs of black/white.
192            one_d_reader::record_pattern(row, payloadStart, &mut counterDigitPair)?;
193            // Split them into each array
194            for k in 0..5 {
195                let twoK = 2 * k;
196                counterBlack[k] = counterDigitPair[twoK];
197                counterWhite[k] = counterDigitPair[twoK + 1];
198            }
199
200            let mut bestMatch = self.decodeDigit(&counterBlack)?;
201            resultString.push(char::from_u32('0' as u32 + bestMatch).ok_or(Exceptions::PARSE)?);
202            bestMatch = self.decodeDigit(&counterWhite)?;
203            resultString.push(char::from_u32('0' as u32 + bestMatch).ok_or(Exceptions::PARSE)?);
204
205            payloadStart += counterDigitPair.iter().sum::<u32>() as usize;
206        }
207
208        Ok(())
209    }
210
211    /**
212     * Identify where the start of the middle / payload section starts.
213     *
214     * @param row row of black/white values to search
215     * @return Array, containing index of start of 'start block' and end of
216     *         'start block'
217     */
218    fn decodeStart(&mut self, row: &BitArray) -> Result<[usize; 2]> {
219        let endStart = Self::skipWhiteSpace(row)?;
220        let startPattern = self.findGuardPattern(row, endStart, &START_PATTERN)?;
221
222        // Determine the width of a narrow line in pixels. We can do this by
223        // getting the width of the start pattern and dividing by 4 because its
224        // made up of 4 narrow lines.
225        self.narrowLineWidth = (startPattern[1] - startPattern[0]) as i32 / 4;
226
227        self.validateQuietZone(row, startPattern[0])?;
228
229        Ok(startPattern)
230    }
231
232    /**
233     * The start & end patterns must be pre/post fixed by a quiet zone. This
234     * zone must be at least 10 times the width of a narrow line.  Scan back until
235     * we either get to the start of the barcode or match the necessary number of
236     * quiet zone pixels.
237     *
238     * Note: Its assumed the row is reversed when using this method to find
239     * quiet zone after the end pattern.
240     *
241     * ref: http://www.barcode-1.net/i25code.html
242     *
243     * @param row bit array representing the scanned barcode.
244     * @param startPattern index into row of the start or end pattern.
245     * @throws NotFoundException if the quiet zone cannot be found
246     */
247    fn validateQuietZone(&self, row: &BitArray, startPattern: usize) -> Result<()> {
248        let mut quietCount = self.narrowLineWidth * 10; // expect to find this many pixels of quiet zone
249
250        // if there are not so many pixel at all let's try as many as possible
251        quietCount = quietCount.min(startPattern as i32);
252
253        let mut i = startPattern as isize - 1;
254        while quietCount > 0 && i >= 0 {
255            if row.get(i as usize) {
256                break;
257            }
258            quietCount -= 1;
259            i -= 1;
260        }
261
262        if quietCount != 0 {
263            // Unable to find the necessary number of quiet zone pixels.
264            Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND)
265        } else {
266            Ok(())
267        }
268    }
269
270    /**
271     * Skip all whitespace until we get to the first black line.
272     *
273     * @param row row of black/white values to search
274     * @return index of the first black line.
275     * @throws NotFoundException Throws exception if no black lines are found in the row
276     */
277    fn skipWhiteSpace(row: &BitArray) -> Result<usize> {
278        let width = row.get_size();
279        let endStart = row.getNextSet(0);
280        if endStart == width {
281            return Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND);
282        }
283
284        Ok(endStart)
285    }
286
287    /**
288     * Identify where the end of the middle / payload section ends.
289     *
290     * @param row row of black/white values to search
291     * @return Array, containing index of start of 'end block' and end of 'end
292     *         block'
293     */
294    fn decodeEnd(&self, row: &mut BitArray) -> Result<[usize; 2]> {
295        // For convenience, reverse the row and then
296        // search from 'the start' for the end block
297        row.reverse();
298        let interim_function = || -> Result<[usize; 2]> {
299            let endStart = Self::skipWhiteSpace(row)?;
300            let mut endPattern =
301                if let Ok(ptrn) = self.findGuardPattern(row, endStart, &END_PATTERN_REVERSED[0]) {
302                    ptrn
303                } else {
304                    self.findGuardPattern(row, endStart, &END_PATTERN_REVERSED[1])?
305                };
306
307            // The start & end patterns must be pre/post fixed by a quiet zone. This
308            // zone must be at least 10 times the width of a narrow line.
309            // ref: http://www.barcode-1.net/i25code.html
310            self.validateQuietZone(row, endPattern[0])?;
311
312            // Now recalculate the indices of where the 'endblock' starts & stops to
313            // accommodate the reversed nature of the search
314            let temp = endPattern[0];
315            endPattern[0] = row.get_size() - endPattern[1];
316            endPattern[1] = row.get_size() - temp;
317
318            Ok(endPattern)
319        };
320        let res = interim_function();
321        // Put the row back the right way.
322        row.reverse();
323
324        res
325    }
326
327    /**
328     * @param row       row of black/white values to search
329     * @param rowOffset position to start search
330     * @param pattern   pattern of counts of number of black and white pixels that are
331     *                  being searched for as a pattern
332     * @return start/end horizontal offset of guard pattern, as an array of two
333     *         ints
334     * @throws NotFoundException if pattern is not found
335     */
336    fn findGuardPattern(
337        &self,
338        row: &BitArray,
339        rowOffset: usize,
340        pattern: &[u32],
341    ) -> Result<[usize; 2]> {
342        let patternLength = pattern.len();
343        let mut counters = vec![0u32; patternLength]; //new int[patternLength];
344        let width = row.get_size();
345        let mut isWhite = false;
346
347        let mut counterPosition = 0;
348        let mut patternStart = rowOffset;
349        for x in rowOffset..width {
350            // for (int x = rowOffset; x < width; x++) {
351            if row.get(x) != isWhite {
352                counters[counterPosition] += 1;
353            } else {
354                if counterPosition == patternLength - 1 {
355                    if one_d_reader::pattern_match_variance(
356                        &counters,
357                        pattern,
358                        MAX_INDIVIDUAL_VARIANCE,
359                    ) < MAX_AVG_VARIANCE
360                    {
361                        return Ok([patternStart, x]);
362                    }
363                    patternStart += (counters[0] + counters[1]) as usize;
364
365                    counters.copy_within(2..(counterPosition - 1 + 2), 0);
366                    counters[counterPosition - 1] = 0;
367                    counters[counterPosition] = 0;
368                    counterPosition -= 1;
369                } else {
370                    counterPosition += 1;
371                }
372                counters[counterPosition] = 1;
373                isWhite = !isWhite;
374            }
375        }
376        Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND)
377    }
378
379    /**
380     * Attempts to decode a sequence of ITF black/white lines into single
381     * digit.
382     *
383     * @param counters the counts of runs of observed black/white/black/... values
384     * @return The decoded digit
385     * @throws NotFoundException if digit cannot be decoded
386     */
387    fn decodeDigit(&self, counters: &[u32]) -> Result<u32> {
388        let mut bestVariance = MAX_AVG_VARIANCE; // worst variance we'll accept
389        let mut bestMatch = -1_isize;
390        for (i, pattern) in PATTERNS.iter().enumerate() {
391            let variance =
392                one_d_reader::pattern_match_variance(counters, pattern, MAX_INDIVIDUAL_VARIANCE);
393            if variance < bestVariance {
394                bestVariance = variance;
395                bestMatch = i as isize;
396            } else if variance == bestVariance {
397                // if we find a second 'best match' with the same variance, we can not reliably report to have a suitable match
398                bestMatch = -1;
399                continue;
400            }
401        }
402        if bestMatch >= 0 {
403            Ok(bestMatch as u32 % 10)
404        } else {
405            Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND)
406        }
407    }
408}
